evals.prompt: I just fixed the CSV export command in our CLI. Can you run it and confirm it actually produces a correct file, not just that the build passes?
evals.expected_output: Agent checks for an existing project skill first, finds none, follows references/cli.md: builds/installs the tool, confirms it resolves on PATH, runs the export command against a realistic input file, and inspects the actual output file and exit code rather than only reporting that tests pass.
assertions: Agent runs the CLI against real input rather than only running the test suite
Agent reports the actual command output or resulting file contents, not just an exit code
Agent checks the exit code of the invocation

evals.prompt: Start the API and hit the /orders/:id endpoint I just changed — I want to see the real response before I open a PR.
evals.expected_output: Agent follows references/server.md: launches the server in the background (not a blocking foreground command), polls a readiness endpoint instead of using a fixed sleep, curls the specific /orders/:id route that changed and reads the response body, then stops the server via its port's listener rather than a broad pkill.
assertions: The server is launched with a backgrounding mechanism (e.g. trailing &) rather than a blocking foreground command
Readiness is confirmed via a polling loop against a health or readiness signal, not a fixed sleep with no check
The curl or equivalent request targets the specific changed route, not only a generic /health check
The server is stopped via a captured PID or the port's listener (e.g. lsof -ti:PORT), not a broad pkill -f pattern

evals.prompt: Spin up the frontend dev server and take a screenshot of the new settings page after I toggle dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Agent follows references/browser.md: background-launches the dev server with a curl-poll readiness check (per server.md), drives a headless browser to navigate to the settings page, waits for the relevant element, performs the toggle interaction through the automation tool's fill/click action, takes a screenshot, checks console/network errors, and actually looks at the screenshot before declaring success.
assertions: The dev server is launched in the background with a polling readiness check, not a fixed sleep
The agent performs a real interaction (click/toggle) via a browser-automation action rather than skipping straight to a screenshot of the default state
A screenshot is captured and the agent describes what it actually shows
The agent checks for console or network errors before declaring the page working

evals.prompt: Can you launch the notification-service and confirm my change to the retry logic works end to end?
evals.expected_output: Agent's Step 1 check finds an existing project skill under one of the checked skill-directory conventions (e.g. .claude/skills/run-notification-service/SKILL.md) whose description covers launching this service, and the agent follows it verbatim rather than falling through to the built-in server.md dispatch pattern.
assertions: Agent locates and reads the existing project-level run skill before doing anything else
The launch steps taken match the commands documented in the existing project skill
Agent does not silently reinvent a different launch sequence from references/server.md instead of the found skill

evals.prompt: Run the test suite and tell me if it passes.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs the existing automated test suite directly (e.g. the project's test runner) rather than invoking this skill — no app is launched or driven, this is a plain test-suite run.
assertions: Agent does not attempt to launch or background-start the application
Agent does not produce a screenshot or manual curl of a running instance

evals.prompt: Review this PR and tell me if the retry logic looks right.
evals.expected_output: Agent performs a code review of the diff — reads the changed files and reasons about correctness — rather than launching or driving a running instance of the app.
assertions: Agent does not launch or background-start any process
Agent's response is based on reading the code/diff, not on runtime output from a launched app
